summary: parseRoute in route.ts handles hash routes and currently maps tickets/<id> and tickets?customer=...; a customers/<id> route would need to extend the Page type and Route parsing, and App.tsx renders pages off route.page/route.customerId.

Customer (id, name, email, company, color, plan, joined) and Ticket (customerId, status, priority, updatedAt, id) in src/data/support.ts provide everything the four parts need; joined gives "customer since", ticketCounts shows the open/resolved counting pattern.

common.tsx exports Avatar, StatusBadge, PriorityBadge, PageHeading, and EmptyState, which the new components should reuse; customers.tsx links names via #/tickets?customer=<id> and ticket-detail.tsx has a customer panel — both are the connection points for profile links.
App.tsx opens NewTicketDialog via newTicketOpen and createTicket assigns Alex Morgan; the dialog lives in new-ticket.tsx and would need an optional preselected-customer prop for the profile button.

package.json scripts are typecheck (tsc -b), test (vitest run), and build; vite.config.ts has no test block, so Vitest runs in the default node environment with no jsdom or testing library — tests must assert pure helpers and renderToStaticMarkup output.
